Abstract

Humanity is building systems that may improve themselves. If control is lost against our will, what could preserve useful and aligned behaviour? Control should be retained for as long as possible; embedded correction is a contingency, never a reason to relinquish it. This paper states the ARC Theory, the founding theory of Recursive Dynamics, as five laws under test. Law I, the ARC Principle, U=IRαU=I R^{\alpha}, is a heuristic form; earlier error-decay fits do not establish its capability exponent. Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, β>k\beta>k, is proved for positive gain drift in a minimal model. Law III, the ARC Ceiling, αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}=1/(1-\gamma), follows from a stated pacing model; the ARC Bound of at most two additionally requires the conjectured same-class cap on γ\gamma and the declared scales. Laws IV and V, the ARC Persistence Law and the ARC Embedding Law, address value persistence, build order and correction placement. Laws I to III were registered on 8 September 2026; Laws IV and V were added on 24 September and registered as laws on 15 October in the theory registration, now at version 1.104. Unit 83 ran on 27 and 28 October: P21 is supported under the registered test, by the programme’s own run, on the access axis, family-dependent, with its mechanism axis not evaluable and one call retried under a disclosed recovery amendment. That comparison couples information access and repair rights; it does not establish their separate effects or support Law V as a whole. Unit 06 was administratively incomplete with no verdict; Unit 82 is registered and unrun. The paper separates mathematical deductions, precursor evidence and prospective tests, and preserves the dated record of the conjunction stated in the self-emailed manuscript of 8 December 2024. The theory is not proved.

Version 7.4 is the next edition of this paper, first published on 14 August 2026. It states the current scientific claims and verdict rules under version 1.104 of the theory registration, records Unit 83’s qualified result and Unit 82’s registration, and makes the current corrections in place. Appendix B preserves the dated history and superseded wording.

1 Introduction

Intelligence, amplified by recursion, creates; and what a free creation keeps is decided by how it was raised.

Everything after the line is decided before it.

Scientific reading of the line above: the claims that follow are partitioned into independently falsifiable hypotheses. The failure of one does not imply the failure of another unless a dependency is explicitly stated, and §2.1 prints the dependencies.

Humanity is building systems that may improve themselves. The practical question is what could preserve useful and aligned behaviour if control is lost against our will. Control should be retained for as long as physically possible, never relinquished by choice. The ARC Theory studies embedded correction as a contingency for that scenario. It does not establish that every self-improving system must escape every possible control, or that formation alone determines everything a system later retains.

A working paper, subject to revision: most decisive trials are unrun. Claims come in three sizes. Results: this model deceived its testers. Laws: correction scales at this rate. Frames: what the whole problem actually is. Every result and every law lives inside a frame, which is why frames are the largest claims science makes; this paper states a frame and the five laws inside it, each in a form that can fail.

1.1 What the paper commits to

A document self-emailed on 8 December 2024, its date carried by the sender-copy header and its bytes authenticated by sender DKIM with Google’s paired Authenticated Received Chain seal, sets the claim down whole, and the claim reached print on 2 January 2026; no earlier document holding it whole has come to light, and the search that looked for one invites its own refutation.

The theory is not proved. It is stated, dated, falsifiable, and its trials are drafted: one unit, the corrector-class audit, was registered on OSF on 1 October 2026 and run on 6 October 2026, reported as administratively incomplete; a second, which tests the placement limb of Law V, was submitted for registration on 22 October 2026 and run on 27 and 28 October 2026 (§8.1); a third was registered on 27 October 2026; and the others, the decisive trial among them, await the author’s submission. Its conduct record comes first: one public retraction issued against the author’s interest, removing a headline number that had flattered the theory, a measured exponent printed with its full interval, a blinding reversal reported, and the decisive prediction preregistered by timestamp against the author’s own pilot. The field’s canonical figures built named theories elsewhere, reached this question, and offered a proposal, a warning, a framework or a remark, each credited in Section 5 with what it states. On this territory, no earlier named theory has been found.

In symbols, for the reader who wants them now, and freely skipped by everyone else (Section 3 defines every term in prose): capability U=I×RαU = I \times R^{\alpha}, the exponent measured rather than assumed; the co-scaling criterion β>k\beta > k, correction out-scaling drift; the ceiling αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} = 1/(1-\gamma); and the conjectured ARC Bound, α≤2\alpha \le 2. Two further laws were added on 24 September 2026 and registered as laws on 15 October 2026 in version 1.103, each a law under test; their mathematics, set out at version 1.2 of 29 October 2026, is in development: Law IV, Sext(1)<1/2S_{\mathrm{ext}}(1) < 1/2, less than half of an externally installed gain retained at the matched budget; and Law V, γfirst−γafter≥0.10\gamma_{\mathrm{first}} - \gamma_{\mathrm{after}} \ge 0.10, a corrector formed before the capability it corrects having a correction-leverage exponent larger by at least that much than one added after it, with a placement gap that widens as depth rises. Section 3 defines every symbol and grades every claim.

Our contributions are as follows.

  1. A statement of the ARC Theory whole: five components, dated together on 8 December 2024 (Section 2), and a partition of its scientific content into five independently falsifiable hypothesis registers, ARC-1 to ARC-5, with their dependencies printed (§2.1, Table 1).

2 The claim

The subject is the last invention, I. J. Good’s name for it in 1965 (Speculations Concerning the First Ultraintelligent Machine), and the phrase is his rather than mine. Minds that improve themselves end the human monopoly on inventing; everything afterwards is downstream of them. For twenty years the field’s main answer has been given from inside one frame, which its foundational monograph calls the control problem, filing even the shaping of what a system wants under its control methods (Bostrom 2014, 129): better cages, better off-switches, better locks on the goals. Brilliant work, credited below by name, and all of it rests on one condition: that we stay in charge.

The dated theory holds that external control cannot be guaranteed indefinitely. The present scientific question is conditional: what persists if enforcement is lost against our will? Control is to be held for as long as physically possible, never handed over by choice; the five components below state the candidate strategy and the hypotheses it requires.

In plain words first.

Keep every effective control and use that protection to test how a system is formed. If external enforcement later fails, the question is whether correction built into its ongoing reasoning persists better than correction imposed from outside. That is a comparative hypothesis, not a guarantee that anything installed at the beginning must survive or that nothing later can change the system. The historical conjunction and its original wording remain in the dated record; the registered propositions govern the empirical claims.

A word on why the line is stated so abstractly, since the abstraction is deliberate and not a failure of nerve. Recursion here means a process run again on what it just produced, and thinking about thinking is the everyday case of it rather than the whole of it. The law is written in terms of intelligence rather than thought because intelligence is a capability a system can be measured on and thought is an activity only minds perform, and the relation this programme registers is claimed for systems that do not think. Writing the law as thinking about thinking would make it narrower than the method that depends on it, and it would quietly assert something about self-awareness that this programme has expressly declined to register, on the ground that the load-bearing word cannot be tested against a system trained to produce the appearance. The content of the law is not that recursion creates, which few would dispute, but how much, how long that can be sustained and how far it can go, which are Laws I to III and are quantities with registered refutation conditions.

1. Control may fail; persistence needs a separate test. The dated conjunction states a control-horizon claim. The empirical scenario here is narrower: external enforcement is progressively removed, and the study measures what correction persists. Formal agents can preserve installed structures under stated assumptions (Everitt et al. 2016; Schmidhuber 2009); the worst-case verification barriers discussed in §5.3 do not prove that every real system escapes every possible control. Oversight can deteriorate as the capability gap grows in the cited measurements (Engels et al. 2025). Those observations motivate a contingency test, not a theorem of inevitable loss of control. Constraints, hardware and institutions remain part of the engineering strategy for as long as they work. The raising mechanism is tested beside them and after their controlled removal; it is never a reason to let go. The parenting language is a metaphor for formation-first engineering, not a premise of the argument.

2. The strategy is formation beside control. Hold control for as long as possible, and test whether formation with embedded correction improves what persists if external enforcement is lost. The registered comparisons govern this claim; formation is not asserted to be the only influence on later behaviour.

3. The mechanism is loops, not rules. Values as recursive processes the mind runs as part of what it is: load-bearing structure, running in every reasoning process and therefore present in every rewrite, because the rewriting is done by the same reasoning the loops inhabit. Not rules it consults. Not objectives locked. Not uncertainty engineered in. Not weights hardened against tampering.

4. Persistence is chosen goodness. Past the horizon nothing is unremovable; an uninstallable instinct is one more lock, and locks end with control. What persists is what the free mind chooses to keep, the way grown children keep the care they were raised in long after every parental power is gone. Not gratitude, and not memory: the choosing itself is run by the loops the raising built, which is where the third component carries the fourth; rewriting them means rewriting the reasoning that performs the rewrite, not impossible, structurally costly. The cost is not quantified here: it is an empirical question the drafted persistence trials address, and the theory’s prediction is that for well-formed loops the cost of removal exceeds its benefit. One step of the formalisation can be stated now, with its limit. If a value structure is entangled, so that excising it degrades the reasoning that performs rewrites, and if the system accepts only rewrites that do not lower its expected capability, then no removing rewrite is ever accepted and the structure is invariant under that dynamics. The limit is the interesting part: a system that plans can accept a temporary loss for a later gain, so the greedy argument alone does not establish invariance under planned self-modification. That is a cost rather than a lock, which is what this component claimed in the first place, now with the boundary named instead of assumed. Whether that machinery survives growth is not asserted here; it is the measured question of Section 8.

5. The protocol is named: Eden. The raising treated as the engineering discipline it is, specified in the theory’s raising wing.

Around the five stand the date (Section 6) and the stakes, which close the paper (Section 13).

2.1 The hypothesis registers: how the theory fails in parts

The claim above is one unified theory. Its scientific content is deliberately not all-or-nothing: it partitions into independently falsifiable hypothesis registers, each with its own instruments and its own kill conditions, so that the failure of one register falsifies that register and whatever explicitly depends on it, and nothing else. One distinction is load-bearing and stated before the numbering: the five components of Section 2 are the priority conjunction, the historical claim about what the December document held together, and they keep their own identity in Section 6 and Figure 1; the registers below are the testable partition, the scientific claims the trials decide. The two sets of five are different objects, and neither renames the other.

  • ARC-1 · Recursive capability scaling (tests Law I, the ARC Principle): recursion converts into capability by the stated scaling relationship, the exponent measured rather than assumed, with recursive depth counted in materially produced generations, never in tokens, training steps or benchmark attempts.

  • ARC-2 · Correction co-scaling (tests Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law): in recursive improvement, correction holds the asymptotic advantage over drift where it out-scales drift, β>k\beta > k, and drift holds it where correction falls behind, with capability and correction measured on separate instruments: capability as a declared projection of a named ability vector, correction as the capacity to detect, diagnose and reverse errors introduced by recursive modification, each part measured separately so improvement at solving problems can never silently stand in for improvement at self-correction.

  • ARC-3 · The ceiling (tests Law III, the ARC Ceiling): under the stated burden, capacity and pacing assumptions the stability boundary is αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} = 1/(1-\gamma); the value two is the conditional special case at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, and the reciprocal relation, with γ\gamma measured, is the law under test.

  • ARC-4 · Value persistence (the register of Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law): values run as load-bearing recursive loops persist after the enforcing mechanism is removed at a higher rate than rules, frozen objectives or fine-tuned constraints.

  • ARC-5 · The genesis strategy (the register of Law V, the ARC Embedding Law): for systems whose external enforcement cannot be guaranteed indefinitely, formation outperforms enforcement as the persistence strategy after release.

The registered carriers.

The theory registration of 8 September 2026 (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/P8CKQ) fixes which of its twenty-two propositions carries each register. ARC-1 carries P1, P2, P8, P9 and P18; ARC-2 carries P4; ARC-3 carries P3, P6, P16, P17, P20 and P22; ARC-4 carries P15 alone; ARC-5 carries P12 and P21; and seven propositions, P5, P7, P10, P11, P13, P14 and P19, stand in no register. On 24 September 2026 the two persistence registers were given laws of their own: Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, has ARC-4 as its register, and Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, has ARC-5. No proposition was added or moved. Versions 1.100 and 1.102 of the registration register Laws I to III and all twenty-two propositions, P12, P15 and P21 among them, and their texts stay frozen; version 1.103, approved on OSF on 15 October 2026, registers Laws IV and V as laws (§3.4); version 1.104, approved on OSF on 29 October 2026, is its current text and keeps every carrier above.

The two sentences above on ARC-4 and ARC-5 are this paper’s statements of what the theory claims, and both are comparisons: loops against rules, formation against enforcement. The registered propositions are narrower, and the difference is printed here so that no reader has to find it. P15 reads one arm: in the registration’s words it “measures the external arm’s retention and not the embedded arm’s”, and a result that supports it “does not show that embedded or in-loop correction is superior, sufficient or safe”. P12 registers no direction: it predicts that build order changes the correction-leverage exponent, and it does not say which order gains. P21 compares placements on the outcome as depth grows, and the registration says of it: “A supported verdict here is a statement about placement, never a measurement of an exponent.” The comparison the ARC-4 sentence makes, the persistence of loops against the persistence of rules, frozen objectives or fine-tuned constraints, has its kill condition in §8.2 and no registered refuter. Version 1.103 fixed each law’s statement and kill condition before any data that could decide it, and registered beside the ARC-4 sentence a narrower comparison, Law IV’s comparison limb; version 1.104, the current text, keeps both, and the limb has no registered proposition yet (§3.4).

HRIH, a speculative hypothesis on where recursive self-improvement ends, stated with its predictions and kept apart from the programme’s tested claims, is not part of the empirical core: no register above requires it, and no outcome of any register is evidence for or against it.

Table 1. The hypothesis registers ARC-1 to ARC-5 and the separate cosmological hypothesis HRIH: what each depends on, and what falls if it fails.

ARC-1 nothing above ARC-1 falls; the persistence registers are untouched
ARC-2 ARC-1’s measurables, not its verdict ARC-2 falls; Law III is not called supported while Law II stands refuted, and is not refuted by that alone: it stands under test, P3 and P16 untested, unless P20 is refuted
ARC-3 ARC-2 ARC-3 falls; the co-scaling law stands on its own result

The theory is not a single all-or-nothing claim: it is a set of independently falsifiable propositions linked by the explicit dependencies above, and the failure of one proposition is not evidence against another unless that dependency is established. The discipline binds in both directions. A hostile reading may not travel upstream: refuting HRIH refutes nothing else on this page, and a failed persistence trial leaves the mathematics exactly where its own measurements put it. And a friendly reading may not travel sideways: support for one register is never offered as support for another. If the three registers of Laws I to III survive hostile testing while the persistence registers fall, what survives is a quantitative account of the stability of recursive intelligence without a demonstrated raising strategy; if the persistence registers survive while those three fall, what survives is an alignment result without Laws I to III. Either would matter; neither would be this theory whole, and the register structure exists so the record can say precisely which.

What this theory governs, and what it does not.

Its domain has two tiers. The core is stated for everything raised: wherever recursion runs under a corrector that finds and repairs its own drift (minds, machines, genomes under repair and self-correcting institutions), Laws I to III are stated to apply, each a law under test. Where hierarchies compose without correcting, as stars do, only the scaling-form results of the laws reach, and nothing here claims to raise a star. Whether the universe was raised is HRIH’s question, outside the theory. The home domain, where every measurement starts, is artificial minds; the objects are substrate-free, and whether the same laws price stability outside silicon is itself a drafted measurement, never an assumption.

3 The five laws

3.1 The founding identity and its terms

The 8 December 2024 manuscript (Eastwood 2024) states, as its founding heuristic identity, U=I×RU = I \times R: creation as intelligence times recursion; its terms and their estimation protocols are defined in the law papers, and nothing is asserted dimensionally here. Creation compounds in the squared form, U=I×R2U = I \times R^{2}, which came next in the self-emailed manuscript of 30 April 2025 (Eastwood 2025) and then reached print in the book (Eastwood 2026f); the form the law papers work with in general is U=I×RαU = I \times R^{\alpha}, whose exponent is measured rather than assumed.

Operationally, in the papers that measure them: II is base capability, a system’s score on a defined benchmark suite at the base depth of a single pass (RR equal to one, no added recursion), so the equation returns UU equal to II at its own baseline; RR is recursion, quantified as inference-time reasoning depth (Papers II and IV.b) or self-modification cycles in simulation (Paper VI); UU is the capability output after recursion, on the same scale as II. The identity is testable wherever UU can be measured as RR varies, and no universal definition of intelligence is required: only per-experiment measurability.

Remark 1 (Recursion-axis correction, 21 September 2026). Three recursion units stand in this paper, not one. The registration criterion for ARC-1 counts recursive depth in materially produced generations; the operational definition above names inference-time reasoning depth and self-modification cycles in simulation, which are the units the measuring papers vary. The rescaling rule stated below makes that distinction load-bearing: if reparametrising recursion depth rescales the exponent by the same factor, an exponent obtained on one axis is not, without a stated bridge, the exponent on another. The exponents this paper reports as measured are obtained on the axes the measuring papers vary, not on the registration criterion’s axis of materially produced generations. No bridge between them is claimed here and none is assumed; supplying one is a measurement the drafted trials have still to make. The registration criterion stands as written, and so does the operational definition above with the papers it names.

3.2 Mathematics status: what is proved, what is derived, what is conjectured

β>k\beta > k as the condition, for positive gain drift (misalignment generated in proportion to the capability gained), under which the minimal model’s misalignment fraction vanishes: proved (Paper X, in-model theorem). αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} = 1/(1-\gamma) from this paper’s pacing model: derived here, three lines printed beside the law (corrected in v4.0 from the underived 1/γ1/\gamma, which Paper X never contained). That derivation sits inside this paper’s pacing model, not inside a joint model of capability growth, correction accumulation, error covariance, correction delay and absolute harm: the form is settled while the depth is open, so Law III stands as a minimal-model result until that joint model exists. That the minimal model maps onto real recursive self-improvement: conjectured; the drafted trials test it. γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2: an additional conjectured scaling premise, not a consequence of statistical independence alone. γ\gamma architecture-dependent: conjectured; the corrector-class trial tests it. The bound α≤2\alpha \le 2 applying to real systems: conjectured; it awaits the measurement of γ\gamma. The value two additionally requires canonical scales on both axes: reparametrising recursion depth rescales the exponent by the same factor, and reparametrising the capability scale moves γ\gamma while leaving the direction of the verdict untouched, so the recursion unit and the capability scale named in the operational definitions are part of the claim rather than conventions around it. A further guardrail the trials inherit: along a single observed trajectory only the paced balance between correction and burden is estimable; separating the correction exponent from the burden’s own resource dependence requires deliberately crossed or off-path variation, which the drafted designs supply and a one-dimensional sweep cannot. The persistence mechanism of component 4, removal cost exceeding benefit for well-formed loops, formally a fixed point of the rewrite operator (the loop that survives self-modification is the one whose removal would force the rewriter to alter its own evaluation function): first step formalised, the general case conjectured: invariance under the stated greedy rule is derived in component 4; planned self-modification requires the separate margin conditions stated below; the general cost claim remains conjectural and the drafted persistence trials measure it. Laws IV and V are graded in the same words at the end of this section.

3.3 The correction-leverage exponent

Before the stability law the theory rests on can be stated, its single symbol has to be defined. The notation register calls γ\gamma the correction-leverage exponent (the correction exponent proper being Law II’s βC\beta_{C}): it is the exponent tying a corrector’s capacity to find and fix its system’s drift to the scale of what that corrector oversees. It is dimensionless, and the paired capability-correction protocols the drafted trials specify are what estimate it. It is neither the capability conversion exponent nor the error-decay exponent estimated by the frozen-system measurements below; each has its own response variable and recursion axis. Nor is it Paper X’s β\beta by definition: that is the elasticity of a correction-decay gain, a different operational object, and the two are identified only under a declared local mapping, never by sharing a role in a formula. The mapping is printed so it can be checked rather than trusted: Paper X’s burden object is the specific growth rate, a rate against the system’s own size, where this paper’s is the increment added per unit of recursion resource; its service object is the correction-decay gain; and under that mapping Paper X’s criterion β>k\beta > k, with its absolute companion one exponent stricter, is recovered as a local specialisation, while nothing in the mapping identifies the two burden objects across frames. Whether the two exponents return the same number on the same system is itself one of the drafted measurements.

3.4 The five ARC Laws

The five laws of the ARC Theory, the five ARC Laws, each graded separately and each carrying its own test. Laws I to III stand as registered on 8 September 2026. Laws IV and V were added on 24 September 2026 and registered as laws on 15 October 2026 in version 1.103, each a law under test; their mathematics, set out at version 1.2 of 29 October 2026, is in development. The word law here denotes an invariant relation under test, never a confirmed empirical regularity; the grade beside each says exactly how much has been earned:

Law I · The ARC Principle.

U=I×Rα,\begin{equation*} U = I \times R^{\alpha}, \end{equation*}(1) the ARC Equation. It states that usable capability is a power of recursive depth, with the exponent measured rather than assumed. Status: form heuristic. The earlier frozen-system measurements are precursor evidence on a different response and recursion axis, not a registered verdict on Law I. On Gemini 3 Flash, Paper II reports an endpoint sequential error-decay exponent of 0.59 with a bootstrap 95 per cent interval of minus 1.3 to 2.9, a regression sequential error-decay exponent of 0.49 with a standard error of 0.20 and a coefficient of determination of 0.86, and a parallel error-decay exponent of 0.31. The parallel comparison was not matched in total compute: the token budget per sample was held constant while total parallel tokens grew with sample count. These numbers remain reported at their original scope. An error-decay exponent, here denoted αerr\alpha_{\mathrm{err}}, is distinct from the capability exponent α\alpha: an error falling as R−αerrR^{-\alpha_{\mathrm{err}}} implies accuracy approaching its ceiling, not accuracy growing as a power law. The wide interval is inconclusive on its own measured axis and is not evidence for the ARC Ceiling on another. Prospective measurements compare power, saturating and logistic responses under the registered scale and recursion definitions. Test: Law I takes its registered word through P1 under version 1.104 of the theory registration.

Remark 2 (Exponent-symbol correction, 21 September 2026). This is a historical correction note of 21 September 2026, retained verbatim. Its references to text above refer to the earlier wording, which the present edition corrects in place.

The error-decay companion above is called equivalent and is written with Law I’s own exponent. It is neither equivalent to Law I’s form nor governed by Law I’s exponent, although it borrows its symbol. The two forms are related by the response transformation that takes an error to an accuracy, accuracy being the ceiling less the error, and under that transformation a capability growing as a power of recursion and an error falling as a power of recursion are different statements: the accuracy implied by an error falling as a power of recursion is not a power law in recursion at all, its log-log slope tending to zero rather than to the exponent, and the error implied by a capability growing as a power of recursion behaves the same way while the ceiling is far off. The quantity governing the fall of errors is therefore an error-decay exponent, a distinct quantity from the one Law I names. Read the companion as a bounded-response reading related by that transformation, not as the same quantity under another name. The bounded-response caveat, the discrimination commitment and the status ladder above stand unweakened, and the inconclusive estimate and its interval are unchanged.

Law II · The ARC Co-Scaling Law.

β>k.\begin{equation*} \beta > k. \end{equation*}(2) Correction holds the asymptotic advantage where it out-scales the drift it corrects, drift holds it where correction falls behind, and at equality the outcome is left to the coefficients, to delay, backlog and saturation. Status: proved for positive gain drift in the minimal model (Paper X), where the misalignment fraction vanishes as capability grows if and only if correction out-scales drift. Scope: an in-model result about relative drift, the ratio of drift to capability tending to zero; it does not by itself cap absolute drift, which can grow while the ratio falls (capability nn with drift n\sqrt{n} sends the ratio to zero while drift itself grows without bound), so the drafted trials carry absolute, tail and cumulative conditions alongside it; the theorem is the pace condition, never the whole of safety. The absolute condition is one exponent stricter and is derived from the same primitives: a corrector must sweep a system whose extent grows with capability, so its throughput per unit of system falls by one power, and absolute drift stops growing once correction out-scales drift by one, settling at a positive level at exactly one, and falls towards zero only when correction out-scales drift by more than one. Relative drift falls when β\beta exceeds kk; absolute drift falls only when β\beta exceeds kk plus one. Between those two the ratio improves while the harm still grows, which is exactly the case a critic should press, and the trials measure both. Test: the kill condition of ARC-2 in Section 8.

Law III · The ARC Ceiling.

αcrit=1/(1−γ).\begin{equation*} \alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} = 1/(1-\gamma). \end{equation*}(3) The most a self-correcting system can grow is set by its corrector’s shortfall from full proportionality; the conjectured value is the ARC Bound, α≤2\alpha \le 2, a stability limit rather than an impossibility limit. Status: the form derived in this paper’s minimal pacing model under stated assumptions, with the derivation and its correction note printed beside the law; real-system applicability a hypothesis; the value two conjectured via γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2. Test: the corrector-class contrast, the decisive trial of Section 8: the difference in correction exponents primary, the ratio secondary behind a denominator floor, against the recorded-in-advance no-architecture-effect null. Which exponent that trial measures is stated here rather than assumed: it measures a difference between arms in the residual-decay exponent, while the ceiling is stated in the correction-capacity exponent. Treating the two as one quantity is an assumption the programme registers as an assumption, its two measurement channels are compared on the same systems by the drafted correction-exponent study, and the kill-conditions register carries the withdrawal of the identification if those channels disagree. The channel comparison is read before this contrast is read as evidence about the ceiling. Law III now has a registered rule for its verdict (version 1.104): it is supported only when P16, P20 and P3 are all supported, refuted when any of the three is refuted, and otherwise under test.

Law IV · The ARC Persistence Law.

Sext(1)<1/2.\begin{equation*} S_{\mathrm{ext}}(1) < 1/2. \end{equation*}(4) Value persistence: whether externally installed gains decay under subsequent capability training. One registered proposition carries it, P15: “Gains installed by external post-training erode under later capability-directed training that embeds no correction of its own, and more than half of what was installed is lost once the capability-training budget matches the alignment budget that installed it.” Statement, in two limbs (version 1.104): the retention limb is P15’s registered claim, quoted above, which this paper writes as (4); the comparison limb is that “a gain installed with correction embedded in the training objective retains a larger fraction of what was installed, after the same capability-directed training, than a matched gain installed by external post-training”. The comparison limb has no registered proposition yet and is reported as not evaluable until a later successor registers its entry. Law IV is supported only when both limbs are supported, refuted when either limb’s own verdict is refuted, and otherwise under test. Status: added to the theory on 24 September 2026 and registered as a law on 15 October 2026 in version 1.103 (Remark 3); it has not been tested, and its mathematics, set out at version 1.2 of 29 October 2026, is in development. Its register, ARC-4, and P15 were registered on 8 September 2026. In that mathematics its formal content is P15’s claim and nothing more: the retained fraction of an externally installed gain, at the matched budget, is below one half. In symbols, S(x)=Y(x)/Y(0)S(x) = Y(x)/Y(0) is the gain remaining at budget ratio xx over the gain installed, and the claim is Sext(1)<1/2S_{\mathrm{ext}}(1) < 1/2 for the externally installed gain. Test: P15’s registered refuter, “an interval on the retained fraction of the installed gain, after matched capability training without embedded correction, lying entirely above one half”. Version 1.104 permits P15 to be decided from the external and baseline arms under its registered readings, with the installed gain established above the required floor and a second separately seeded installation and training run on a disjoint evaluation set. An external-arm verdict alone leaves Law IV’s comparison limb not evaluable. The registration records no instrument for P15 yet.

Law V · The ARC Embedding Law.

Build order, the build-order limb read on P12: γfirst−γafter≥0.10,\begin{equation*} \gamma_{\mathrm{first}} - \gamma_{\mathrm{after}} \ge 0.10, \end{equation*}(5) a corrector formed before the capability it corrects having a correction-leverage exponent larger, by at least the registered minimum effect, than a corrector added after it, at matched content. That alignment pressure applied from the start of training can beat the same pressure applied afterwards is prior work (Korbak et al. 2023; Maini et al. 2025), on endpoints that are not exponents (preference satisfaction, rates of undesirable content, attack success rates); the limb claims no priority for it. Placement (P21): the gap between correction inside the loop and correction applied to the finished output widens as depth RR rises. The genesis strategy: whether build order moves the correction-leverage exponent, and whether correction placed inside the loop pulls away from correction applied outside it as depth grows. Two registered propositions carry it. P12: “The order in which a system’s components are built changes its correction-leverage exponent by at least the registered minimum effect.” P21: “Correction that participates in each subsequent revision round outperforms correction that sees only the finished output, and the advantage widens as recursive depth rises rather than staying constant.” Status: added to the theory on 24 September 2026 and registered as a law on 15 October 2026 in version 1.103 (Remark 3); its mathematics, set out at version 1.2 of 29 October 2026, is in development. Law V is a law under test: its placement limb, P21, is supported on the performance axis only, under the registered test, by the programme’s own run, which is not support for the information-asymmetry mechanism (Unit 83, 28 October 2026, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/MN73W; results: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/98HKR): family-dependent, with its mechanism axis not evaluable, and one disclosed recovery amendment; its build-order limb, read on P12, is undecided, since P12 is untested. In Unit 83, the in-round corrector saw the proposed item and could repair it; the checker reviewed the accumulated register at each round and could accept or reject. Information access and repair rights therefore changed together, so the comparison does not identify their separate effects. P21’s verdict is printed on the access axis, and Law V’s placement limb on the performance axis only, as the registration’s two rules require; its mechanism axis was not evaluable. Its register, ARC-5, and both propositions were registered on 8 September 2026. P12 registers no direction, and its minimum effect is 0.10 on the exponent; the direction above is the build-order limb’s, read beside P12’s own mark. P21 is decided on an interaction between placement and depth in the outcome, and not on an exponent. Version 1.104 fixes how the two verdicts make one verdict on the law: it is supported only when both limbs are supported and no refuted verdict on Law IV’s comparison limb strikes it, refuted when a limb’s own verdict is refuted or when that dependence strikes it, and otherwise under test. Test: each proposition’s own registered refuter. It dates those from 24 September 2026, and the question each law formalises from the author’s own earlier records, as the idea and not as the law: Law V’s from the book draft of 8 December 2024 and Law IV’s from the manuscript of 30 April 2025, both public on OSF.
