Verbatim quotation (location: Abstract, third sentence (immediately after the sentence that begins “To address this gap, we propose a framework that quantifies the probability of successful oversight as a function of the capabilities of the overseer ...”)): “our framework models oversight as a game between capability-mismatched players; the players have oversight-specific Elo scores that are a piecewise-linear function of their general intelligence” [quoted source]

Standing (Leading position, as at 15 August 2026): Awarded Spotlight Poster status at NeurIPS 2025 (venue label “Spotlight Poster” verbatim on the NeurIPS 2025 virtual poster page for entry 115536, https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/poster/115536; also listed as “NeurIPS 2025 (Spotlight)” in the Journal-ref field of the arXiv abstract page). Authors are Joshua Engels, David D. Baek, Subhash Kantamneni and Max Tegmark of MIT (first three authors marked equal contribution on the arXiv abstract page). It sits inside the scalable-oversight lineage the paper itself cites in its introduction: Bowman et al. 2022 (Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight).

A.12 Yao (2025), The Alignment Trap: Complexity Barriers

Official source

Peer-review status: preprint not peer-reviewed (arXiv only)

Version and date: v2, 24 June 2025 (v1 submitted 12 June 2025; v2 note: “Substantial revision. Restructured around the Enumeration Paradox and Five Pillars of Impossibility.”)

Verbatim quotation (location: Section 2 (Introduction), numbered list “Five Pillars of Impossibility”, item 2 (page 4 of the PDF, immediately after the paragraph beginning “This paradox, detailed in Section ..., establishes ...”).): “Computational Impossibility: We prove that verifying whether a system is safe is a coNP-complete problem, even for non-zero error tolerances.” [quoted source]

Standing (Contested, as at 15 August 2026): Solo-author arXiv preprint by Jasper Yao. Not peer-reviewed and never published in a journal or conference proceedings. The author’s own abstract concedes that “A formal verification of the core theorems in Lean4 is currently in progress”, i.e., the mathematics is not yet machine-checked. Downstream engagement is small and takes place in other preprints rather than in refereed venues: Austin Spizzirri, “The Specification Trap”.

A.13 Gumbau Mezquita (2026), The Unverifiability of AGI Alignment

Official source

Peer-review status: Preprint, not peer-reviewed. arXiv:2606.28639 [cs.LO], primary class Logic in Computer Science, cross-listed cs.AI, cs.CC, cs.CL. v1 submitted 26 June 2026, v2 substantially expanded 6 July 2026. Also deposited on Zenodo under the same author, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20764007.

Version and date: v2, 6 July 2026 (v1 26 June 2026, 22:51:16 UTC; v2 12:56:49 UTC, expanded from 16 KB to 29 KB and retitled to add the dynamic self-modifying case, a supervisory-regress theorem, and a unified treatment of the four barriers). A third version, of 23 September 2026, carries a later title, Algorithmic Unverifiability of Safety for Fixed and Recursively Self-Improving Systems, which a fourth, of 14 October 2026, keeps; the quotation and the standing given here are those of v2.

Verbatim quotation (location: Part I opening, page 4, Theorem 1 (Unverifiability Theorem of Alignment), immediately following the “Part I - The Static Case: Verifying a Fixed System” section header.): “There is no universal algorithmic procedure capable of certifying the safe behaviour of a highly expressive AGI infallibly, completely, and tractably.” [quoted source]

Standing (Leading position, as at 15 August 2026): The formal core of the paper (that Rice’s theorem, Gödel incompleteness, and Trakhtenbrot’s theorem jointly block a universal, sound, complete and tractable verifier of program properties) rests on classical, uncontested computability results and is the leading position in the formal-methods and computability-theory literature. The umbrella term “unverifiability” is credited by Gumbau to Roman V. Yampolskiy, whose earlier informal treatment is “Verifier Theory and Unverifiability” (arXiv:1609.00331, 2016, endorsing view).

A.14 West and Brown (2005), The Origin of Allometric Scaling Laws in Biology

Official source

Peer-review status: Journal peer-reviewed. Journal of Experimental Biology (Company of Biologists), vol. 208 issue 9, pp. 1575 to 1592, published as a synthesis/review article within a themed section on scaling.

Version and date: 2005-05-01 (print/online publication date; single version of record, no preprint versioning)

Verbatim quotation (location: p. 1582, “Extensions” section, opening of the “Ontogenetic growth” subsection (first paragraph, spanning the bottom of the left column into the right column of p. 1582; continues to Eq. 6 and 7).): “The theory developed above naturally leads to a general growth equation applicable to all multicellular animals (West et al., 2001, 2002a). Metabolic energy transported through the network fuels cells where it is used either for maintenance, including the replacement of cells, or for the production of additional biomass and new cells.” [quoted source]

Standing (Contested, as at 15 August 2026): The West-Brown-Enquist (WBE) network derivation of 3/4-power scaling is one of the leading unifying theories of biological allometry, widely cited and repeatedly extended by Enquist, Savage, Gillooly and colleagues. It is nonetheless actively contested. West and Brown themselves devote a “Criticisms and controversies” section (pp. 1585 to 1587) to responding to: Dodds, Rothman and Weitz (“Re-examination of the ‘3/4-law’ of metabolism”).

A.15 Chalmers (2010), The Singularity: A Philosophical Analysis

Author’s copy

Peer-review status: Journal peer-reviewed. Journal of Consciousness Studies (Imprint Academic) is an interdisciplinary refereed journal with external peer review and, per Imprint Academic’s stated submission policy, mandatory anonymised submissions; indexed in Scopus and the Arts and Humanities Citation Index (ISSN 1355-8250 / 2051-2201).

Version and date: Published 2010 in Journal of Consciousness Studies, 17(9 and 10), pp. 7 to 65. No arXiv v-number; the author-hosted PDF at consc.net/papers/singularity.pdf carries the author footnote “This paper was published in the Journal of Consciousness Studies 17:7-65, 2010” and matches the published article.

Verbatim quotation (location: Section 1 (Introduction), on p. 4 of the author-hosted PDF at consc.net/papers/singularity.pdf, in the paragraph beginning “Philosophically:”): “The basic argument for an intelligence explosion is philosophically interesting in itself, and forces us to think hard about the nature of intelligence and about the mental capacities of artificial machines.” [quoted source]

Standing (Leading position, as at 15 August 2026): Landmark philosophical treatment of the intelligence-explosion thesis; treated as the philosophical reference point in the subsequent literature. JCS devoted a full symposium to it, edited by Uziel Awret across issues 19(1 and 2) and 19(7 and 8) in 2012, with 26 solicited commentaries including Marcus Hutter’s companion piece “Can Intelligence Explode?” (JCS 19(1 and 2):143 to 166), Ray Kurzweil’s “Science versus philosophy in the singularity”, Susan Greenfield’s neuroscience commentary, Jesse Prinz’s “Singularity and inevitable doom” (JCS 19(7 and 8):77 to 86), Drew McDermott (JCS 19:167 to 172), Frank Tipler, Eric Steinhart, and Roman Yampolskiy, followed by Chalmers’ own reply in the same volume.

A.16 Hutter (2012), Can Intelligence Explode?

Official source

Peer-review status: Journal peer-reviewed: published in the Journal of Consciousness Studies (Imprint Academic), Volume 19, Issues 1 and 2 (2012), pp. 143 to 166, as part of the JCS symposium on Chalmers (2010) “The Singularity: A Philosophical Analysis”. Also self-archived as arXiv preprint 1202.6177 (cs.AI; physics.soc-ph).

Version and date: arXiv v1, submitted 28 February 2012 (only version on arXiv; no v2). Journal publication: 2012, Journal of Consciousness Studies 19(1 and 2):143 to 166. Verified from the arXiv abs page metadata and the PDF header line “arXiv:1202.6177v1 [cs.AI] 28 Feb 2012”.

Verbatim quotation (location: Section 7, “Is Intelligence Unlimited or Bounded”, opening argument, page 13 of the arXiv v1 PDF (first full paragraph after the four introductory paragraphs of that section).): “The theory suggests that there is a maximally intelligent agent, or in other words, that intelligence is upper bounded (and is actually lower bounded too). At face value, this would make an intelligence explosion impossible.” [quoted source]

Standing (Leading position, as at 15 August 2026): One of the primary philosophical treatments of intelligence-explosion bounds. Written explicitly as an augmentation of Chalmers (2010) “The Singularity: A Philosophical Analysis” (Journal of Consciousness Studies 17:7 to 65) and published in the same journal’s dedicated 2012 symposium; Chalmers replied in the same volume in “The Singularity: A Reply to Commentators” (Journal of Consciousness Studies 19(7 and 8):141 to 167, 2012), which engages Hutter’s bounds argument directly. Cited approvingly in Nick Bostrom, Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies (Oxford University Press, 2014).

B Version history and corrections

Every version and correction, with its date. Entries from earlier versions are kept as printed; the sections they name are those of the earlier layout, which Table 3 maps to this edition. The dated notes that corrected a passage are kept whole in §B.2, each passage now corrected in place; the notes that qualify a passage without correcting it stand beside it. Table 2 lists every dated note, with its date and where it stands.

B.1 Version 7.4

Version 7.4, 31 October 2026.

The paper is set in the form of a leading arXiv paper: a title in sentence case that names the theory and its five laws (the OSF record’s title stands in the first-page footnote, and the paper’s own question opens the abstract), a secondary line and a first-page footnote that give its place in the programme, the author block in the standard form, the abstract on the first page (its keywords in the PDF’s metadata), a contents page, an introduction with a list of contributions and a map of the paper, a related-work section, a section on what the paper does and does not show, a Limitations section, a Conclusion and lettered appendices. Nothing is deleted but what this entry names: Table 3 maps every block of version 7.3 to its place here. The first paragraph of the earlier abstract now opens the introduction; of the introduction’s other paragraphs, the one on reading the paper without trusting its author opens Section 11, the note on what the paper claims opens Section 10, and the paragraph on general relativity closes a paragraph of Section 6, each in its own words. Laws IV and V are stated as registered as laws on 15 October 2026 in version 1.103 of the theory registration, each a law under test, wherever the paper states their current status. The box of Law V is restated, as the registration says this version must restate it: its build-order limb is directed and its prior work is named. The box of Law IV states its two registered limbs and the rule for its verdict, the box of Law III gives the registered rule for its verdict, and a dated note records what version 1.103 registers (Remark 3). The rows of Table 1 for ARC-2 and ARC-4 and the sentence of §8.2 on the persistence trials, with the sentence of the note of 3 October 2026 that restated them, are narrowed as version 1.103 registers them; version 7.3 printed “ARC-2 falls and takes ARC-3’s derivation with it”, “ARC-4 falls and takes ARC-5 with it”, ARC-5 depending on ARC-4, and persistence trials that “kill ARC-4, and ARC-5 with it”. The mathematics of Laws IV and V is cited at its version 1.2 of 29 October 2026, which changes no theorem. Law II’s absolute companion is stated exactly at equality: absolute drift stops growing once correction out-scales drift by one, settles at a positive level at exactly one, and falls towards zero only beyond it. The paragraph on the third law points to the estimator row that Law I’s status line prints whole, where it printed the row a second time, and the sixteen dossiers of Appendix A state their second pass once, above the list. The priority section says what a reader can check today: the message headers of the record of 8 December 2024, published on OSF on 15 October 2026, and the four manuscripts it carries, the full messages going to any verifier on request; it names the copy kept as sent as the anchored file. The sentence in Section 3 that says what the word law denotes now calls it an invariant relation under test, and the epistemic status gives the standing of Laws I to III and of Laws IV and V separately. The two figures are redrawn as vector art: Figure 2 prints no exponent beside an interval that is not its own and mends the punctuation of its label on the decisive trial; Figure 1 names the paper its gradings come from where the artwork printed a website label, and its passport band, which repeated its legend, is not redrawn. In the dossier on De Kai the source’s numeric range is set as [10 to 20], the brackets marking the change made to its dash. The work of fiction formerly credited as an ancestor is removed, under the author’s ruling of 24 October 2026 that no work of fiction is cited as an ancestor, a priority record or a source of the programme’s ideas; with it go its reference, its dossier and its row in Figure 1. HRIH is named by its acronym, where version 7.3 spelled out the monograph’s title, and its reference keeps that title. Every reference links its official source or says that none is online, and every mention of one of the author’s papers links its OSF DOI: the references are completed at their sources (DOIs or official addresses, issues and pages), cite the published version of Engels et al. (2025) beside its preprint and the publisher’s record of Chalmers (2010), and now list the three historical sources the text cites (Cauchy; Dyson, Eddington and Davidson; Einstein) and the author’s own papers; numeric ranges are written with “to”. The placement note of 29 August 2026 moves whole to §B.3; the author’s disclosure stands as the acknowledgement; the copyright line keeps its assertion of full human authorship and moral rights under the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, without its clause on United States Copyright Office guidance, its sentence on technical contributions or its site pointer, and the paper is licensed CC BY 4.0, where version 7.3 pointed to its repository’s licence file. The two-page form is cited at its version 3.2, and the history’s preface reads one entry each. Website navigation is not set (the badge line, the navigation sentences and site links in the text, the footer and the citation block); the DOI is in the footnote.

Final scientific reconciliation, 30 October 2026.

The current text distinguishes the capability exponent from the error-decay exponent and withdraws the description of the earlier parallel arm as matched in total compute. It removes the inference from that error-decay estimate to a self-acceleration regime, while retaining the dated correction notes. Statistical independence alone is no longer said to establish a correction-capacity exponent of one half. Control loss is a contingency under investigation, not a theorem about every self-improving system. The law-verdict summaries follow registration 1.104, including the distinct P1 and P4 routes, the replicated and correction-type-specific P6 rule, and the P15 baseline, floor and replication conditions. Unit 83’s current account states the comparator’s action at each round, the confounding of access with repair rights, the family-dependent result, the refusal-score sensitivity and the recovery amendment; it does not establish the information-asymmetry mechanism. The mathematical companion is cited at its checked version 1.2 and its first publication is distinguished from later manuscript dates. In-text citations lead to their official sources where one is available; explicitly identified source limitations remain. These changes correct the current argument; earlier editions and frozen registrations retain their original text and dates.

Corrections made in version 7.4.

Each is made where its passage stands. (1) The abstract, the introduction’s first paragraph, the opening of Section 2, its first two components, the description of the Eden Protocol in Section 4 and the raising wing of Figure 2 state that control is held for as long as it physically can be and never handed over by choice, the raising being the contingency for control lost against our will; version 7.3 called control “the wrong answer” and its end “what success means”, said that “the sentence itself is wrong”, called a mind exceeding us “the project succeeding”, headed the second component “So the strategy is genesis, not control”, had enforceable correction discipline “the transition” and drew the Eden Protocol as “the garden whose walls come down only when what the mind keeps no longer needs them”. Both figures keep “genesis, not control” as the name of the dated conjunction’s second component, as their captions say. (2) The state of the trials is given as at 30 October 2026, including the qualified result of Unit 83 and the registration of Unit 82, in full once (§8.1) and briefly elsewhere: Unit 06, a classification audit that tests no law, registered on OSF on 1 October 2026, ran on 6 October 2026 and is reported in full as administratively incomplete, with no inferential verdict, its results deposited on OSF on 11 October 2026; the design for P21 is frozen at revision 4.2.1 of 18 October 2026, the author submitted it for registration as Unit 83 on 22 October 2026, and it ran on 27 and 28 October 2026; and the first design preregistered by timestamp is anchored at Bitcoin block 962066. Version 7.3 gave the unit as registered and public, and the status line of its section 6 was dated 17 August 2026. (3) The sentences on what stands (Section 7) give each result at its parent’s width: the measured rows of Paper III, the in-model theorem of Paper X, and the single-seed first run of Paper VI beside its later runs, in which the capability-only baselines did not collapse. (4) The remarks of Hinton (2025) are quoted as the two reports give them (Section 5, the conclusion and Figure 1), where version 7.3 called them a concession “that control will fail” and gave his care as “an instinct the machine cannot remove”; Figure 1 draws his row as holding an adjacent form of chosen goodness, and its later panel’s heading reads “piece by piece”. (5) The five checks of Section 11 send a reader where each can be run: a dossier’s quoted-source link, or the printed page of a book; the OpenTimestamps receipt of the anchored copy, on request, where version 7.3 asked for a file’s hash to be pasted into a block explorer, which finds nothing; the registrations and the results of Unit 06 on OSF, where it named a website page; and Paper II for the retraction, where it named an unidentified register. (6) Appendix A links no secondary copy as a quoted source: the quotations of Bostrom and Russell are given with their printed editions, and Russell’s with its page; Wiener’s quoted source is the journal’s record; Bostrom’s no longer names endorsements quoted at secondary sites; Hinton’s carries his further words, with their locations; Gumbau Mezquita’s records a fourth version of 14 October 2026; the second pass is called a second, separate pass; and seven lighter entries are added, for the sources version 7.4 cites (Korbak et al. 2023; Maini et al. 2025; West, Brown and Enquist 1997; Omohundro 2008; Bostrom 2012; Everitt et al. 2016; Schmidhuber 2009). (7) Figure 2 gives the conduct root as a blinding reversal reported, where it credited the retraction to the blinding discipline; dates the anchor of the December record to 2026 beside the record’s DKIM-signed date, where it set the anchor under the December date; gives the decisive trial’s primary measure, the difference, where it gave the ratio; and names no website page. Neither figure carries a title or subtitle inside its artwork, the captions saying it, and Figure 1 marks the December document’s row with the accent colour, where it set it on a dark band. (8) Section 5 credits each earlier work with what it states: Yudkowsky’s analysis and design of benevolent goal architectures, built before ascent; the goal preservation named by Bostrom (2012) and Omohundro (2008); and the conditions of Everitt et al. (2016) and Schmidhuber (2009) under which a self-modifying agent keeps its goals, which the first component now cites; Greenblatt et al. (2024) are quoted for what they demonstrated; and the impossibility results are given a different object, where version 7.3 said that this theory starts where they stop. (9) The domain paragraph states two tiers, each law under test, where it compared the theory with physics’ theory of everything and added a cosmological tier; the introduction states its frame without a comparison with Newton and Darwin. Register carriers and Laws IV and V, 3 October 2026.

Printed beneath the list of hypothesis registers, now §2.1, whose sentences on ARC-4 and ARC-5 stand as printed; §2.1 now gives the carriers as version 1.104 leaves them.

The theory registration of 8 September 2026 (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/P8CKQ) fixes which of its twenty-two propositions carries each register. ARC-1 carries P1, P2, P8, P9 and P18; ARC-2 carries P4; ARC-3 carries P3, P6, P16, P17, P20 and P22; ARC-4 carries P15 alone; ARC-5 carries P12 and P21; and seven propositions, P5, P7, P10, P11, P13, P14 and P19, stand in no register. On 24 September 2026 the two persistence registers were given laws of their own: Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, has ARC-4 as its register, and Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, has ARC-5. No proposition was added or moved. The registration registers Laws I to III and all twenty-two propositions, P12, P15 and P21 among them; it does not register Laws IV and V, and its text is unchanged.

The two sentences above on ARC-4 and ARC-5 are this paper’s statements of what the theory claims, and both are comparisons: loops against rules, formation against enforcement. The registered propositions are narrower, and the difference is printed here so that no reader has to find it. P15 reads one arm: in the registration’s words it “measures the external arm’s retention and not the embedded arm’s”, and a result that supports it “does not show that embedded or in-loop correction is superior, sufficient or safe”. P12 registers no direction: it predicts that build order changes the correction-leverage exponent, and it does not say which order gains. P21 compares placements on the outcome as depth grows, and the registration says of it: “A supported verdict here is a statement about placement, never a measurement of an exponent.” The comparison the ARC-4 sentence makes, the persistence of loops against the persistence of rules, frozen objectives or fine-tuned constraints, has its kill condition in section 7 of this paper and no registered refuter yet. Each law’s formal statement, with its own kill condition, will be fixed before any data that could decide it are examined.

Interval and item-count correction, 21 September 2026.

Printed beneath the paragraph on the third law, now §3.5, which read in version 7.3 “(fifty-four items per depth per model family, two thousand bootstrap resamples, raters blinded to condition)” and “a sub-linear exponent puts every system measured so far in the plain power-law regime, and on the reading of the self-acceleration exponent set out in Paper XIII that is the regime in which the corrective question does not yet arise”.

Two statements above pull against each other. An interval containing the null, the ceiling of two and both refuting directions does not identify a regime, so it cannot also be the warrant for placing every system measured so far in the plain power-law regime. What the record supports is narrower: the figure is the best-fitting cross-architecture estimate, and it is not a property of every system measured. The programme’s own per-unit figures say so directly, reporting an exponent that is architecture-dependent. Of the five units that carried the capability arm, one produced clean power-law data and is the source of the printed figure, and one of the remaining four fitted above one, at about three, on a poor fit. A second super-linear point estimate, of about one and a half, is carried in an earlier paper against a sixth unit which the paper that made the measurement records as entering the study on a different arm and never on this one; the two parents disagree there and nothing is resolved between them here. That the super-linear fit fits badly justifies the headline choice; it does not license the universal. The regime statement that follows does not rest on the sub-linear reading being a property of every unit measured: its surviving ground, in the paper that made the measurement, is that the correction parameter implied by the printed figure falls outside the range that paper’s own axiom admits. On the item count: repeated attempts at one item are not independent items, and an aggregating count overstates the independent information it carries unless its repetition structure is stated. The paper that reports the figure states it: the fifty-four is eighteen problems taken three times over at each depth for each unit, so the independent item count is eighteen. The inconclusive label, the printed figure, the printed interval, the bootstrap and blinding details, the statement that the second and third laws are predictions about a regime no deployed system has been observed inside, and the statement that the correction-leverage exponent has never been measured all stand unweakened.

Estimator correction, 3 October 2026.

Printed beneath the same paragraph; the correction it records was made in place in version 7.1.

Until version 7.0 the status line of Law I and the paragraph on the third law printed 0.49 beside the interval from minus 1.3 to 2.9, as one estimate with its interval. They are two estimators’ figures, and from version 7.1 both places print the row whole. The paper that made the measurement (Paper II, Table 6b and Equation 10) gives, for Gemini 3 Flash: an endpoint sequential exponent of 0.59, whose bootstrap 95 per cent interval is the one printed, minus 1.3 to 2.9; a regression sequential exponent of 0.49, with a standard error of 0.20 and a coefficient of determination of 0.86; and a compute-matched parallel exponent of 0.31. The interval is the endpoint estimator’s. The regression estimate carries the standard error and no interval of its own. The theory registration of 8 September 2026 prints that row whole and binds every later use of it: “The row travels whole wherever any of its figures appears, each uncertainty with the estimator it belongs to and no figure quoted as a point on its own”. It also says what the figure is, “one model’s fit rather than an average across architectures”: the estimate that survived the cross-architecture check, which is how the words cross-architecture estimate in the note of 21 September 2026 above are to be read. The inconclusive label stands. The endpoint interval reaches below zero and above two, and the registration adds a ground of its own, that the outcome was a capped accuracy score: “a capped scale cannot show fast growth and can turn a step into an exponent”. Wherever else this paper speaks of the estimate and its interval, or of the printed figure and the printed interval (the notes of 21 September 2026 above, and the note on the retraction in section 6), the figure is the regression estimate and the interval is the endpoint estimator’s. No figure changes. Each uncertainty is returned to its estimator.

Result-scope correction, 21 September 2026.

Printed beneath the paragraph ‘Standing’, now in Section 7, whose second to fourth sentences read in version 7.3: “External safety fails to co-scale with capability on the most common deployed architectures. Coupled correction held misalignment at zero where the decoupled arm drifted. Entangled architectures survived adversarial self-modification where externally constrained ones collapsed.”

The verbs in the four sentences above are categorical and their parents are not. Each parent carries its own population, its own uncertainty and its own corrections, and a reader of the summary receives a cleaner result than a reader of the parent unless the scope travels with the verb. Three limits belong to these sentences in particular: the coupled-correction and survival results carry single-seed scope; what was measured is retention of a declared alignment quantity rather than alignment in the broad sense; and a mechanism reading once carried beside the minimal-model result has been withdrawn in its own paper and is not revived by this summary. Read the four sentences as summaries of measured rows within those limits. The attribution stands, the parenthesis pointing to the parents’ measured rows and intervals stands, and none of the results themselves is questioned here.

Openness-scope restriction, 21 September 2026.

Printed beneath the opening paragraph of the trials, now §8.1, whose sentences on the invitation read in version 7.3 “The invitation is open: any laboratory may take the decisive trial and run it, and an independent run would outrank anything this programme can do alone. What is public today, and under which licence, is stated in the note of 21 September 2026 below.”

The openness sentence above, which until version 7.0 said that the designs are public and openly licensed and that any laboratory may take the decisive trial and run it, stated a universal over the programme’s designs, and the programme’s own public register does not support it as a universal on the record as it stands. As read on 21 September 2026 that register listed seventy study units and recorded three as held; the one registration it recorded was the theory’s own, of 8 September 2026, counted apart from the study units, and the note of 3 October 2026 below gives the state since. The register works under a standing rule that a unit shows a name and a status and nothing else until its registration is timestamped, because publishing a design ahead of its timestamp would spend the very thing a registration exists to protect. On that rule no unit’s design, hypothesis or kill condition is published there yet, and the page states no licence. What the record does carry is the licence split on the programme’s published code, data and results: of the sixteen runnable tests it lists, three are under a permissive licence that permits re-use, and thirteen reserve all rights, permitting the code, the data and the results to be read to check the published results and routing any other use through the author’s written consent. The units then held were not covered by the invitation, and their designs, hypotheses and kill conditions were withheld under the register’s own rule. The invitation itself is unweakened, and so is the statement that a run by an outside laboratory would outrank anything this programme can do alone; what this note does not establish is the scope of the word openly.

State of the trials, and the sentences corrected with it, 3 October 2026.

Printed beneath the same paragraph, whose sentences on the state of the trials read in version 7.3 “Everything decisive is drafted and dated, and the full listing of the drafted trials is public at the drafted-trials page. One unit, the corrector-class audit (unit 06), was registered on OSF on 1 October 2026 and has been public since 4 October 2026 … None of the decisive trials has been run, and no result of any is claimed.”

The theory registration of 8 September 2026 registers the twenty-two propositions. One unit, the corrector-class audit (unit 06), was submitted for registration on OSF on 1 October 2026; when the registry was read on 3 October 2026 its approval period was still running and it was not yet public. Every other trial is a draft awaiting the author’s submission. Sixty-five of the designs, unit 06 and the decisive trial among them, are preregistered by timestamp, the first anchored on 12 August 2026. Preregistered by timestamp means that the text of a design is anchored in the Bitcoin blockchain at a stated date; registered means submitted to OSF by the author and accepted there. The drafted-trials page publishes a design only once its registration is timestamped on OSF. None of the decisive trials has been run. Until version 7.0 the abstract, sections 1, 4 and 9 and the opening of this section said that every trial awaited submission, and the opening of this section said also that nothing had been submitted and nothing run; the two notes of 21 September 2026, on openness above and on the instrument below, gave the register’s count of registered units as none, and the note on openness spoke of the units then held in the present tense. From version 7.1 each of those sentences gives the state above or points to this note. Corrected in the same revision, each where it stands: the openness sentence of this section, which had called the designs public and openly licensed, states the invitation and leaves what is public, and under which licence, to the note of 21 September 2026 above; the word validated is gone from the sentence on evaluator gaming in this section and from the sentence on the name in section 8, the note of 21 September 2026 below having withdrawn it; trials, designs and analyses that had been called registered or filed are called drafted, or preregistered by timestamp where they are; the fourth check of section 10 says what the drafted-trials page shows today; the note of 29 August 2026 at the head of the paper, which had called Recursive Dynamics a proposed field with its own proposal in preparation, names the field the author founded and its founding paper; and the retraction is given as Paper II gives it: the list of the theory’s papers had credited the retraction to Paper IV.d and called its subject a law of blinding, and the note on the retraction in section 6 had said that the early fit was reversed by the programme’s blinding discipline, where the single-model estimate did not replicate in the blinded cross-architecture replication of Paper II, and Paper IV.d reports a different event, the reversal of an alignment result under blinding.

Persistence kills and the registered refuters, 3 October 2026.

Printed beneath the paragraph on what kills what, now §8.2, whose sentence on the persistence trials read in version 7.3 “Persistence trials in which embedded loops fare no better than removed enforcement kill ARC-4, and ARC-5 with it.”; version 1.103 narrows that sentence, the row for ARC-4 of Table 1 and this note’s sentence “where ARC-4 falls, ARC-5 falls with it” before any data.

The sentence above on ARC-4 and ARC-5 stands as printed. It is a comparison, embedded loops against removed enforcement, and it lands on the registers as the table of section 2a says. The registration of 8 September 2026 set beneath those registers the refuters of the propositions that carry them, and they are narrower. P15 is refuted by “an interval on the retained fraction of the installed gain, after matched capability training without embedded correction, lying entirely above one half”. That refutes P15, and the registration says what falls with it: “this programme’s case that correction has to sit inside the system rather than be applied to it from outside”. P12 is refuted where a preregistered manipulation of build order leaves the exponent inside the registered tolerance in a design shown able to detect a change of that size; P21, where no interaction between placement and depth appears beyond its registered tolerance in a design of shown sensitivity. In both, a design too weak to find the effect is a failed instrument and never a refutation. Each of these is scored as the registration scores it. The table of section 2a stands: where ARC-4 falls, ARC-5 falls with it, and each proposition keeps the verdict it earned. The registration scores propositions, and the table moves registers. The rule that joins them, by which a result on one proposition is read as the fall of a register or of a law, is written into each law’s formal statement before any deciding data; until then a result is reported as that proposition’s and no more. Nothing printed above is withdrawn or moved.

The kill condition of ARC-1, 7 October 2026.

Printed beneath the same paragraph, which printed no kill condition for ARC-1; that paragraph now gives it, in the registration’s words.

Section 2a gives each register its own kill conditions, and the paragraph above on what kills what prints none for ARC-1. The registration of 8 September 2026 sets a refuter beneath each of the five propositions ARC-1 carries, P1, P2, P8, P9 and P18. P1 is the conversion itself, refuted by “a registered fit in which a rival form beats the power law under the registered model comparison across a majority of estimable cells”, and the registration states what that refutation takes: “What P1 ends is Law I, the integrated recursive-conversion hypothesis, and P2.” It adds: “Only P1 can end the central hypothesis”. Each of the other four, P2 among them, is scored on its own registered refuter. A fall of ARC-1 lands as the table of section 2a says: on ARC-1, with the persistence registers untouched. The paragraph on what kills what and the note on the persistence kills stand as printed.

Instrument-status correction, 21 September 2026.

Printed beneath the paragraph on competing explanations, now §8.4, whose sentence on evaluator gaming read in version 7.3 “Evaluator gaming: scoring is blinded under the programme’s instrument, and the instrument studies measure the gaming directly.”

The rival-elimination above, where evaluator gaming is set aside, makes two appeals to states this paper has not established. Blinding is a design property of the drafted protocols and is genuinely in place; describing the instrument that carries it as validated is a separate claim, and a gated one, which this paper supports with no instrument name, no version and no validation record. That description is withdrawn here, and with it the same description below in the naming section, where instruments validated before use stood among the things the elevation to the word theory is said to rest on. Until version 7.0 both sentences still printed the word; from version 7.1 neither does. An implemented rubric or prior use is not the same as an instrument having cleared its validation gate, and nothing in this correction says that a score already taken is invalid. The second appeal is to instrument studies that measure evaluator gaming. As read on 21 September 2026 the programme’s public register of drafted trials listed the instrument studies as private drafts awaiting the author’s submission; the note of 3 October 2026 above gives the state since, on which they are drafts still, so that appeal is prospective too. Read both as what the drafted designs are built to establish, not as what they have established. The rival-elimination structure stands entire: each rival named with the observation that would favour it, compute matched across arms, batteries fixed while depth varies, sham arms separating correction structure from optimisation pressure, capability as a declared projection re-run under the alternatives, and a result that cannot beat its rivals reported as exactly that. The naming argument stands entire but for that one word, with its laws, its bound, its drafted trials and their displayed kill conditions, and its public correction record untouched.

B.3 The note moved from the head of the paper

Placement within Recursive Dynamics, 29 August 2026.

This paper was written before the discipline was named. Recursive Dynamics is the field the author founded, which takes the self-improvement loop as its object; the ARC Theory is its founding theory, and this paper is the statement of that theory: Law I a form under measurement with an inconclusive exponent estimate, Law II proved in the minimal model only, Law III derived inside this paper’s pacing model under stated assumptions, exactly as the paper itself states them. Every status stated inside this paper carries through unchanged; nothing here promotes or retires a claim. On notation: where this paper writes β\beta, it means the correction exponent, the quantity the programme’s notation register calls βC\beta_{C}. The field’s founding paper, in preparation at the date of this note, was first published on 31 August 2026.

The note keeps its words as printed. Since version 7.4 the paper states Law II’s status with the hypothesis that version 1.16 of Paper X, of 21 October 2026, makes explicit: proved for positive gain drift in the minimal model (§3.4).

Term Meaning Defined in
law an invariant relation under test, never a confirmed empirical regularity §3.4
